title: Recombination Lifetime Explorer
description: Three linked panels for radiative, Shockley-Read-Hall, and Auger recombination in an n-type semiconductor at 300 K: a band diagram showing each path's share of the recombination rate, the decay of the excess carrier density with time, and carrier lifetime against doping for each mechanism and in total.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics
carrier recombination
minority carrier lifetime
Shockley-Read-Hall recombination
Auger recombination
radiative recombination

educational.topic: Recombination mechanisms and minority carrier lifetime
learningObjectives: Identify which recombination mechanism dominates at a given doping and injection level
Calculate the minority carrier lifetime from the trap density and capture cross section
Explain why the position of the trap level affects SRH recombination
prerequisites: Equilibrium carrier concentrations and the law of mass action

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with three linked real-time views and a readout strip; optional animation of transitions
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students calculate the SRH lifetime, then explore how doping, injection, and trap position change the dominant mechanism
assessmentOpportunities: Calculate the lifetime for a given trap density and compare with the readout
Map the doping ranges over which each mechanism dominates in Si and GaAs
Explain the lifetime increase when the trap moves away from midgap

controls.label: Start / Pause
controls.purpose: Animate transitions on the band diagram; the simulation loads paused

controls.label: Trap level Et - Ei
controls.purpose: Trap energy relative to the intrinsic level

controls.label: Injection level dn/n0
controls.purpose: Excess carrier density relative to the equilibrium majority density

equations: U_SRH = (np - ni^2)/(tau_p0 (n + n1) + tau_n0 (p + p1)), tau_0 = 1/(sigma v_th Nt)
n1 = ni exp((Et - Ei)/kT), p1 = ni exp((Ei - Et)/kT)
assumptions: GaAs: ni = 2.1e6 cm^-3, B = 1e-10 cm^3/s, Cn = Cp about 1e-30 cm^6/s
sigma_n = sigma_p = 1e-15 cm^2, v_th = 1e7 cm/s, one trap level
limitations: GaN omitted because its radiative and Auger coefficients are not well established
Constant coefficients; no surface recombination or bandgap narrowing
